item.title: Presley Gerber, son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber, dies at 27
item.description: Presley Gerber, the son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber, has died at 27, a family spokesperson has confirmed.

item.title: ICE agent shoots and wounds man in Austin, Texas
item.description: The lawyer for the man identified him as a 28-year-old Venezuelan national, Wilber Rafael Garces Perez. Officials said he was shot at least once in the torso and was in serious but stable condition.

item.title: Trump to meet Mamdani in New York City on Monday
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and President Trump have met at least twice since Mamdani was elected last year.

item.title: 60 Minutes Transcript: Patrick Clancy
item.description: Patrick Clancy speaks about his ex-wife Lindsay's trial, his grief and moving forward while facing intense public scrutiny.

item.title: Bessent meets with Chinese counterpart ahead of Trump-Xi summit
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, ahead of the planned summit between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping this week.

item.title: Star Trek tech catches up with present day
item.description: This month marks 60 years since the first episode of Star Trek aired on TV, and Dave Malkoff shows how all these years later, the future is now.

item.title: Patrick Clancy opens up about grief, his children and moving forward
item.description: In the first interview since his ex-wife's murder trial, Patrick Clancy describes what happened at home before his children were killed and how he handled his grief in the aftermath.

item.title: Alberta to vote on whether to stay a part of Canada
item.description: The Canadian province of Alberta, a major supplier of oil and natural gas to the U.S., will vote next month on a possible referendum that could break up the country. Ian Lee reports from Raymond, Alberta.

item.title: Newsom signs "Jay Leno's Law," allowing classic cars to hit the streets for short trips
item.description: California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a bill known as "Jay Leno's Law," allowing high-emission classic cars to hit the streets for short trips. Adam Yamaguchi has more details.

item.title: Sheeran says situation in Gaza is "catastrophic and unjustifiable" at Philly show
item.description: Ed Sheeran opened his solo concert in Philadelphia on Saturday with comments about Gaza, saying what is happening there is "catastrophic and unjustifiable."

item.title: Ed Sheeran resumes tour with no openers: "I'm so, so sorry"
item.description: This weekend, British pop star Ed Sheeran resumed his concert tour in Philadelphia, with no openers, amid a world of controversy. Jared Ochacher reports from outside Lincoln Financial Field.

item.title: Tariffs, inflation, trade wars taking toll on American farmers
item.description: America's farmers face a tough harvest this year with trade wars, tariffs and inflation all taking a toll. The cost of diesel hit a new record, averaging $6.50 a gallon, nearly a dollar higher than last month. Lana Zak reports from North Liberty, Iowa.

item.title: Trump faces pressure as midterms inch closer
item.description: President Trump triggered a showdown over the First Amendment after several journalists had their White House access revoked this weekend. The ban followed a week of bad economic news for the president. Aaron Navarro reports.

item.title: 60 Minutes Transcript: The data center uproar
item.description: As tech companies race to develop artificial intelligence, developers are forging ahead with data centers. But the boom is facing backlash from communities.

item.title: Data center developers want to make it hard to track them: elected official
item.description: Data center construction is booming, with many more planned for rural America. But there's also growing tension between economic development and community pushback.

item.title: 60 Minutes Transcript: Shergar, a missing horse, an enduring sports mystery
item.description: Shergar's kidnappers asked for 2 million pounds in exchange for the racehorse's return. Shortly afterward, the kidnappers claimed the horse was dead. Decades later, the search for answers endures.

item.title: Data center opposition a rare issue uniting Americans across the political divide | 60 Minutes
item.description: As tech companies race to develop artificial intelligence, developers are forging ahead with data centers. But the boom is facing backlash from communities.

item.title: Kidnapping of prized racehorse still unsolved decades after he was taken
item.description: Armed men kidnapped Shergar, a prized stallion, from a stud farm in Ireland one night in 1983. They made ransom calls before going quiet. Decades later, no body has been found, and no arrest was ever made.

item.title: Patrick Clancy: The 60 Minutes Interview
item.description: Patrick Clancy speaks about his ex-wife Lindsay's trial, his grief and moving forward while facing intense public scrutiny.

item.title: 9/20/2026: Patrick Clancy; AI Data Centers; Shergar, Where are you?
item.description: First, Patrick Clancy: The 60 Minutes Interview. Then, data center plans boom despite heavy backlash. And, inside the unsolved kidnapping of Shergar.

item.title: Ariel Levy wishes cellphones would go the way of cigarettes in public | 60 Minutes
item.description: New 60 Minutes contributor Ariel Levy doesn't like the attachment people have to their cellphones in public. "What I miss the most is the concentration we used to bring to daily life," she says.

item.title: No body, no arrest: What happened to kidnapped Irish racehorse Shergar? | 60 Minutes
item.description: Shergar's kidnappers asked for 2 million pounds in exchange for the racehorse's return. Shortly afterward, the kidnappers claimed the horse was dead. Decades later, the search for answers endures.

item.title: 9/20: CBS Weekend News
item.description: Global threats impact the U.S. economy as the midterms loom; record U.S. diesel prices squeeze farmers.

item.title: UMass Dartmouth football player killed in stabbing, student charged with murder
item.description: A UMass Dartmouth football player was killed in a stabbing in Providence and another student has been charged with murder.

item.title: Trump says proposed arch will also be a "top grade Military Complex"
item.description: President Trump said that he has agreed to convert plans for a massive triumphal arch into a "top grade Military Complex," equipped with snipers and drone storage.

item.title: 9/20: Face The Nation
item.description: This week on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," President Trump faces a pivotal week ahead in foreign policy as the House is recessed until after the midterm elections. Reps. Ro Khanna and Maria Elvira Salazar join, as well as Sen. Bill Cassidy.

item.title: U.S. embassies across Middle East issue security alerts for Americans
item.description: The alerts did not cite a specific threat, but called for Americans to "exercise heightened vigilance."

item.title: Retiring Smithsonian head Lonnie G. Bunch III: "You can run from history, but you can't hide"
item.description: In 2019, Bunch became both the first historian and the first African American to serve as Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution. As he prepares to retire, he talks about the museums' mission to protect history, and give America a full picture of itself.

item.title: Pentagon releases UFO files with documents on secretive military program
item.description: The Pentagon on Friday released a new group of files about unidentified anomalous phenomena, or UAP or UFOs, including a batch of documents regarding a mysterious military program studying aerospace threats.

item.title: Patrick Clancy's wife: "I don't understand how the story's been so twisted"
item.description: Ross Douthat's interview with Patrick Clancy and his wife, Dr. Rachel Danis, airs Sunday on 60 Minutes.
